A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching methods, experiments, nine figures, four tables, and Appendices A.1–A.10. Text, equations, tables, and graphics are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 and Pythia experiments measuring subnetwork correlations, activation structure, parameter overlap, ablation losses, and text generations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports explicit overlap-significance outcomes across the models in Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: Continuous sparsification, the cross-entropy-plus-sparsity objective, masking exclusions, and optimal-subnetwork construction remain unchanged. Added explanations of bigram estimation and embedding exclusions document the existing method rather than establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use English OSCAR data for the same bigram prediction, language modeling, and mechanistic evaluation tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added; the newly specified corpus size describes existing bigram estimation.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same full-model, random-subnetwork, optimal-subnetwork, and embedding-control comparisons. Newly cited circuit research is discussed but not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Previously stated model configurations, checkpoints, sparsity settings, training hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, and evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged. The new bigram-estimation and randomization-test descriptions disclose previously unspecified details without establishing a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: The checkpoint, embedding-patching, activation-rotation, covariance, overlap, ablation, and generation analyses are retained. Appendix A.9 elaborates statistical reporting for the existing overlap analysis rather than introducing a distinct ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: v1 reports overlap significance without explaining its calculation. v3 A.9 specifies 10,000 random mask pairs preserving parameter counts within each block and an overlap-tail comparison. This adds statistical-method reporting; it does not establish increased training repetitions or new seed-based uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All plotted and tabulated values and sample generations remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 newly reports zero exceedances among 10,000 random pairs and p < 0.0001 for all five models; v1 explicitly states that significance threshold only for Pythia 1B in Section 6.2.

T1.justification: The loss equation, linear-map and rotation reasoning, and circuit definitions and implications in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. The added randomization-test description supplies statistical details without introducing a new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The empirical claims and four listed contributions remain intact. The abstract and introduction modestly narrow the novelty framing: v3 acknowledges earlier empty-circuit sufficiency evaluations and emphasizes building more complex circuits on a bigram foundation, softening v1's contrast with traditional ablation.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds a speculative account of early bigram heuristics developing into integrated computations. Appendices A.2 and A.4 add explanations involving rare-token masking and non-embedding parameters activating embedding-held information. The caution about intermediate bigram predictions already existed in v1 A.5.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies unsmoothed bigram estimation from 1.28B OSCAR tokens, comprising 10M sequences of 128 tokens, using each model's tokenizer. A.9 documents the overlap-test implementation. Existing hardware, optimization, stopping criteria, and code/subnetwork access information are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds references on interventions and circuit sufficiency, including Conmy, Hanna, Marks, and Mueller, and explicitly credits prior empty-circuit evaluations. This refines the distinction concerning circuit composition; Section 2's positioning around n-grams, sparsification, and residual-stream research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally revises the abstract and introduction, expands the discussion and several appendix explanations, and makes small copyedits. The main section and appendix sequence remains intact. The preprint footer is replaced with a NeurIPS 2025 conference footer.

P2.justification: The figures and tables retain their content and designs. Appendix tables are repositioned: Table 2 moves before the A.4 discussion, and Table 3 moves from alongside Figure 9 to a separate page. Other changes primarily involve text reflow and pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through explicit bigram-estimation details in A.2 and significance-test documentation in A.9. It also qualifies the novelty framing and clearly labels its added mechanism explanation as speculative. These improve transparency and interpretation while leaving the method and main experimental evidence unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
